summary: Kuno Fischer was a philosopher who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1844–1845) and the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1845–1847). He held posts at Heidelberg University (~1850–1907) and the University of Jena (~1856–1872).

Philosopher Kuno Lorenz studied at Tübingen, Hamburg, Bonn, Princeton, Kiel (PhD ~1958–1961), and Erlangen-Nuremberg (Habilitation ~1965–1969). He held a chair of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

Kuno Meyer worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (~1879–1881) and held posts at the University of Liverpool (~1884–1911) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1911–1919).

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Kuntala Bhattacharya completed an MA supervised by Prabal Kumar Sen and a PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra (attested 2009). She held a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).
Kunzang Namgyal studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Terton Sogyal.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and Patrul Rinpoche. He taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

Kurt A. Behrendt works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1991–1997) and became Assistant Curator of Asian Art at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (~2005).
Kurt Andrew Johnson, a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology, completed his PhD at the University of York under the supervision of Jane Moody by 2010.

Kurt Huber studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and earned a PhD at the University of Munich (~1913–1917). Working in philosophy and other fields, he served at the University of Munich as außerordentlicher Professor (1926) and Professor (1938).

Kurt Tropper works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctoral degree at the University of Vienna (-2001) under Ernst Steinkellner, Michael Torsten Much, and Tashi Geisler, holding posts at Vienna as Vertragsassistent and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies Kurtis R. Schaeffer earned degrees at Lewis & Clark, Evergreen State, Washington, and Harvard. He held faculty posts at the University of Alabama (2000, 2004) and the University of Virginia (2005).
Kurunegoda Piyatissa worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as the head of the New York Buddhist Vihara (attested 1998) and was associated with the institution through at least 2009.

Kwangsoo Park works in Buddhist and religious studies. After completing an MA at the University of Iowa and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he served as a professor at Wonkwang University (attested 2020).

Kyo Kano studied at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna. A scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies, Kano was an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and an Associate Professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).

Buddhist studies scholar Kyojun Shimizudani studied under Keijun Shimizudani and at Taisho University (-1915). He served as professor at Taisho University (1919; 1926–1945), head of Senso-ji (~1952–1979), and held posts at Imperial Household Ministry Training Institute and Hieizan Junior High.

Kyoko Fujii studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1978). In Buddhist studies and Indology, she held professorships at Yokohama City, Hamamatsu, Hokkaido, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, also holding leadership roles at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and IIBS.
Kyoko Tokuno works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held positions at the University of Oregon and the University of Washington, where she was an attested professor in 2017.

Kyokuga Saeki studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Gen'yū, Ryoga, and Kasho Noyama. Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he served as the 143rd abbot of Sennyu-ji from around 1877 to 1891.

Kyosho Hayashima worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as lecturer at Yokohama City University (attested 1962), associate professor at Toyo University (attested 1962), and professor at the University of Tokyo (attested 1980).
Kyosho Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1966–1976). He served as an associate professor at Musashino University from around 1976 to 2013.
